title: SDK: default retry budgeting, chunked-stream resume heuristics, and portable idempotency hints
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem statement:
Teams using Redwood SDKs (Python/TS/Go) ask for simple, safe defaults for retries that work both for short synchronous calls and long-lived token streams. Current cross-SDK guidance is fragmented: some SDKs retry aggressively, others leave it to users. We need a single source of truth for: retry budgeting (per-request and per-session), backoff presets by latency tier, streaming resume heuristics for chunked/long-running responses, and a lightweight, portable idempotency hinting approach that plays well with streaming resume and multi-language SDK ergonomics.

Goals:
- Define default retry budgets (max attempts, total retry budget per logical request/session) with clear rationale for cost vs. availability trade-offs.
- Provide three backoff profiles (latency-sensitive, balanced, cost-sensitive) with tunable params and concrete default numbers.
- Specify streaming resume heuristics: when to checkpoint, how to surface resume tokens, dedupe windows, and safe checkpoints in the presence of partial model outputs.
- Design a minimal, language-agnostic idempotency hint scheme (opaque client-provided id + optional per-chunk nonce) and migration paths for existing id-key patterns.
- Produce canonical examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go that demonstrate API ergonomics and recommended snippets for callers.

Non-goals:
- Changing server-side retry semantics or API wire contract.
- Replacing advanced customer-specific policies (we'll provide knobs but not remove existing overrides).

Acceptance criteria:
- A single design doc and PRs implementing defaults in python/ts/go SDKs with feature flags disabled-by-default in runtime for one week canary.
- End-to-end integration test covering: sync generation with transient network error -> retry budget enforcement; streaming generation with mid-stream resume token -> resume completes without duplication; idempotent create call deduplicated within dedupe window.
- Telemetry hooks added: retry_count, retry_reason, resume_used, idempotency_key_present.

Risks & mitigations:
- Overly aggressive retries increase cost: mitigate via conservative default budgets and a cost-sensitive profile.
- Resume ambiguity causing duplication: mitigate by requiring explicit resume token agreement between client and server and recommending per-chunk checksums where available.
- Cross-language ergonomics inconsistency: include simple language-specific helpers and unit tests to ensure parity.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc merged to docs/sdks/retry-budgeting.md and sign-off by SDK leads
Default presets implemented behind feature flags in python/ts/go SDKs with unit/integration tests
Telemetry events added and wired to Console tracing for beta users
Three example snippets (python/ts/go) added to quickstart and included in SDK READMEs

implementation_notes: Implementation will add a RetryBudget class in each SDK that attaches to request/context objects. Streaming helpers will expose resume_token (opaque string) and a resume() helper that verifies dedupe window before replay. Defaults: latency-sensitive (max_attempts=2, initial_backoff=50ms, max_backoff=250ms, jitter=0.2), balanced (max_attempts=3, initial_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=1s, jitter=0.25), cost-sensitive (max_attempts=1, initial_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=2s, jitter=0.1). Deduplication safety window default 45s. All numbers configurable via SDK constructor or per-call options.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for RetryBudget arithmetic and edge cases
- Integration tests simulating transient 5xx, network timeouts, and HTTP 409 conflict (non-retriable)
- Streaming tests cover mid-stream disconnect and resume flow with dedupe window enforcement
- Telemetry sanity tests ensure events emitted with correct tags
notes: Recommend feature gated rollout: enable flags in SDKs + server-side opt-in for resume handshake for first 2 weeks.
Follow-up epic to surface retry budget and resume usage in Console per customer (suggested as product ticket PM-4123).
Consider a small docs playbook outlining migration from current id-key conventions to new portable idempotency hints.
